title.raw: 卷七十六 列傳第二十六: 太宗諸子 Volume 76 Biographies 26: Taizong's Sons

sentences.zh: =褚遂良=

translations.literal: =Chu Suiliang=
translations.idiomatic: Chu Suiliang

sentences.zh: 褚遂良，散騎常侍亮之子也。

translations.literal: Chu Suiliang was the son of Chu Liang, Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Suiliang was the son of Chu Liang, who had served as Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 太業末，隨父在隴右，薛舉僭號，署為通事舍人。

translations.literal: At the end of the Daye reign, he followed his father in Longyou; Xue Ju usurped a title and appointed him Master of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Daye era he accompanied his father in Longyou. When Xue Ju declared himself ruler, he appointed Suiliang Master of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 舉敗歸國，授秦州都督府鎧曹參軍。

translations.literal: When Ju was defeated he returned to the realm and was made Army-Armor Section Staff Officer in the Qinzhou Area Command.
translations.idiomatic: After Xue Ju's defeat he submitted to the Tang and was appointed Army-Armor Section staff officer under the Qinzhou area command.

sentences.zh: 貞觀十年，自秘書郎遷起居郎。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Zhenguan he moved from Secretary to Diarist of the Imperial Presence.
translations.idiomatic: In 636 he was promoted from secretary to diarist of the imperial presence.

sentences.zh: 遂良博涉文史，尤工隸書，父友歐陽詢甚重之。

translations.literal: Suiliang was broadly versed in letters and history and especially skilled at clerical script; his father's friend Ouyang Xun greatly valued him.
translations.idiomatic: Suiliang was widely read in literature and history and was especially accomplished in clerical script. Ouyang Xun, a friend of his father, held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 太宗嘗謂侍中魏徵曰：「虞世南死後，無人可以論書。

translations.literal: Taizong once said to Palace Attendant Wei Zheng: "After Yu Shinan died, there is no one with whom I can discuss calligraphy.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong once said to Palace Attendant Wei Zheng, "Since Yu Shinan died, I have had no one with whom to discuss calligraphy.

sentences.zh: 」徵曰：「褚遂良下筆遒勁，甚得王逸少體。

translations.literal: " Zheng said: "Chu Suiliang's brushwork is forceful and vigorous and very much captures Wang Yishao's style.
translations.idiomatic: " Wei Zheng replied, "Chu Suiliang's brushwork is vigorous and forceful and captures the manner of Wang Xizhi very well.

sentences.zh: 」太宗即日召令侍書。

translations.literal: " That same day Taizong summoned him to attend at writing.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor summoned him that same day to serve at court as a calligrapher.

sentences.zh: 太宗嘗出御府金帛購求王羲之書跡，天下爭齎古書詣闕以獻，當時莫能辯其真偽，遂良備論所出，一無舛誤。

translations.literal: Taizong once brought out gold and silk from the imperial storehouse to purchase traces of Wang Xizhi's writing; all under Heaven vied to bring ancient books to the court as tribute, and at the time none could distinguish true from false—Suiliang fully discussed their provenance without a single error.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong once offered gold and silk from the imperial treasury to buy works attributed to Wang Xizhi. People across the empire rushed ancient writings to court as gifts, and at the time no one could tell authentic pieces from forgeries. Suiliang identified the provenance of each work he examined without a single mistake.

sentences.zh: 十五年，詔有事太山，先幸洛陽，有星孛於太微，犯郎位。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year an edict ordered rites at Mount Tai; the emperor first visited Luoyang; a broom star appeared in Supreme Palace Enclosure and encroached on the Gentlemen's Quarters.
translations.idiomatic: In 641 an edict ordered ceremonies at Mount Tai. The emperor first traveled to Luoyang, where a comet appeared in the Supreme Palace Enclosure and crossed the Gentlemen's Quarters.

sentences.zh: 遂良言於太宗曰：「陛下撥亂反正，功超前烈，將告成東嶽，天下幸甚。

translations.literal: Suiliang said to Taizong: "Your Majesty has quelled disorder and restored the right, your achievements surpassing former worthies; you are about to announce completion at the Eastern Marchmount—the realm is greatly fortunate.
translations.idiomatic: Suiliang said to Taizong, "Your Majesty has quelled chaos and restored order, and your achievements surpass those of earlier sages. You are about to announce completion of your mandate at Mount Tai, to the great fortune of the realm.

sentences.zh: 而行至洛陽，彗星輒見，此或有所未允合者也。

translations.literal: Yet upon reaching Luoyang a comet promptly appeared—perhaps something is not yet in accord.
translations.idiomatic: Yet upon reaching Luoyang a comet appeared at once. This may mean that something is still out of accord with Heaven.

sentences.zh: 且漢武優柔數年，始行岱禮，臣愚伏願詳擇。

translations.literal: Moreover Emperor Wu of Han hesitated for several years before performing the rites at Dai; this humble subject bows and wishes Your Majesty to choose carefully.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Emperor Wu of Han deliberated for years before he finally performed the rites at Mount Tai. I humbly beg Your Majesty to consider the matter with care.

sentences.zh: 」太宗深然之，下詔罷封禪之事。

translations.literal: " Taizong deeply approved and issued an edict halting the Feng and Shan ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: " Taizong was deeply persuaded and issued an edict canceling the Feng and Shan ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 其年，遷諫議大夫，兼知起居事。

translations.literal: That year he was moved to Censor and concurrently managed the affairs of the imperial diary.
translations.idiomatic: That year he was promoted to censor and concurrently supervised the imperial diary.

sentences.zh: 太宗嘗問：「卿知起居，記錄何事，大抵人君得觀之否？

translations.literal: Taizong once asked: "You manage the imperial presence—what do you record? May a ruler in general view it?
translations.idiomatic: Taizong once asked, "As diarist of the imperial presence, what do you record? As a rule, may the sovereign read it?

sentences.zh: 」遂良對曰：「今之起居，古左右史，書人君言事，且記善惡，以為鑑誡，庶幾人主不為非法。

translations.literal: " Suiliang replied: "Today's diarists of the presence are the ancient left and right historians; they write the ruler's words and affairs and also record good and evil as a mirror and warning, so that the lord may not act unlawfully.
translations.idiomatic: " Suiliang replied, "Today's diarists of the imperial presence are the ancient left and right historians. They record the ruler's words and deeds, noting both good and evil, so that these may serve as a mirror and a warning and the sovereign may be kept from unlawful conduct.

sentences.zh: 不聞帝王躬自觀史。

translations.literal: One does not hear of emperors and kings personally viewing the histories.
translations.idiomatic: I have never heard of an emperor or king reading the histories in person.

sentences.zh: 」太宗曰：「朕有不善，卿必記之耶？

translations.literal: " Taizong said: "If I have something not good, will you surely record it?
translations.idiomatic: " Taizong said, "If I do something wrong, will you be sure to record it?

sentences.zh: 」遂良曰：「守道不如守官，臣職當載筆，君舉必記。

translations.literal: " Suiliang said: "Keeping the Way is not as good as keeping one's office; my duty is to bear the brush—whatever the lord does must be recorded.
translations.idiomatic: " Suiliang said, "Upholding the Way is less important than upholding one's office. My duty is to hold the brush: whatever the sovereign does, I must record it.

sentences.zh: 」黃門侍郎劉洎曰：「設令遂良不記，天下亦記之矣。

translations.literal: " Vice Director of the Yellow Gate Liu Ji said: "Suppose Suiliang did not record it—the realm would still record it.
translations.idiomatic: " Vice Director of the Yellow Gate Liu Ji said, "Even if Suiliang did not record it, the realm would still record it.

sentences.zh: 」太宗以為然。

translations.literal: " Taizong considered this correct.
translations.idiomatic: " Taizong agreed that this was so.

sentences.zh: 時魏王為太宗所愛，禮秩如嫡。

translations.literal: At the time the Prince of Wei was loved by Taizong, his ritual and rank like those of the legitimate heir.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Prince of Wei was a favorite of Taizong, and his ceremonial treatment and stipend matched those of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 其年，太宗問侍臣曰：「當今國家何事最急？

translations.literal: That year Taizong asked the attending ministers: "What matter is most urgent for the state today?
translations.idiomatic: That year Taizong asked his attending ministers, "What is the most urgent matter for the state today?

sentences.zh: 」中書侍郎岑文本曰：「《傳》稱『導之以德，齊之以禮』，由斯而言。

translations.literal: " Vice Director of the Secretariat Cen Wende said: "The Commentary says 'Lead them with virtue, regulate them with ritual'—from this speaking,
translations.idiomatic: " Vice Director of the Secretariat Cen Wende said, "The Analects says, 'Guide them with virtue and align them with ritual.' From that perspective,

sentences.zh: 禮義為急。

translations.literal: ritual and righteousness are urgent.
translations.idiomatic: ritual and righteousness are what matter most.

sentences.zh: 」遂良進曰：「當今四方仰德，誰敢為非？

translations.literal: " Suiliang advanced and said: "Today the four quarters look up to your virtue—who would dare do wrong?
translations.idiomatic: " Suiliang stepped forward and said, "Today the four quarters look up to your virtue. Who would dare do wrong?

sentences.zh: 但太子、諸王，須有定分，陛下宜為萬代法以遺子孫。

translations.literal: Only the crown prince and the princes must have fixed stations; Your Majesty should make a model for ten thousand generations to leave to posterity.
translations.idiomatic: But the crown prince and the other princes must have clearly fixed ranks. Your Majesty should establish a precedent for all generations to come and leave it to your descendants.

sentences.zh: 」太宗曰：「此言是也。

translations.literal: " Taizong said: "This statement is correct.
translations.idiomatic: " Taizong said, "That is true.

sentences.zh: 朕年將五十，已覺衰怠。

translations.literal: I am nearing fifty and already feel decline and weariness.
translations.idiomatic: I am nearly fifty and already feel my strength failing.

sentences.zh: 既以長子守器東宮，弟及庶子數將五十，心常憂慮，頗在此耳。

translations.literal: Having already set the eldest son to guard the vessel in the Eastern Palace, younger brothers and sons by concubines number nearly fifty—my heart is constantly anxious, and it lies largely in this.
translations.idiomatic: I have already installed my eldest son as heir in the Eastern Palace, yet my younger sons and sons by concubines number nearly fifty. What weighs on my mind is largely this.

sentences.zh: 但自古嫡庶無良佐，何嘗不傾敗國家？

translations.literal: Yet since antiquity, when legitimate and secondary lines lacked good assistants, when did they not overturn and ruin the state?
translations.idiomatic: Yet since antiquity, when the lines of legitimate and secondary sons lacked good advisers, has the state not been overturned?

sentences.zh: 公等為朕搜訪賢德，以傅儲宮，爰及諸王，咸求正士。

translations.literal: You gentlemen should search out the worthy and virtuous for me to tutor the heir's palace, and likewise for all the princes—seek upright men for all.
translations.idiomatic: Search out worthy and virtuous men to tutor the heir apparent, and do the same for all the princes. Find upright men for every one of them.

sentences.zh: 且事人歲久，即分義情深，非意窺窬，多由此作。

translations.literal: Moreover, when one serves a person for many years, the bond of duty grows deep; illicit schemes for the throne often arise from this.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, when officials serve a prince for many years, their bond of loyalty grows deep, and many plots against the throne arise from just such attachments.

sentences.zh: 」於是限王府官僚不得過四考。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he limited princely household officials to no more than four performance reviews.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon he decreed that officials in princes' households might serve no more than four terms before rotation.

sentences.zh: 十七年，太宗問遂良曰：「舜造漆器，禹雕其俎，當時諫舜、禹者十餘人。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year Taizong asked Suiliang: "Shun made lacquer vessels and Yu carved his stands—at the time more than ten men remonstrated with Shun and Yu.
translations.idiomatic: In 643 Taizong asked Suiliang, "Shun had lacquer vessels made, and Yu had his sacrificial stands carved. More than ten men remonstrated with Shun and Yu at the time.

sentences.zh: 食器之間，苦諫何也？

translations.literal: Over mere eating vessels—why such earnest remonstrance?
translations.idiomatic: Why such strenuous remonstrance over mere eating vessels?

sentences.zh: 」遂良對曰：「雕琢害農事，纂組傷女工。

translations.literal: " Suiliang replied: "Carving and polishing harm agricultural affairs; brocade and embroidery injure women's labor.
translations.idiomatic: " Suiliang replied, "Carving and polishing harm farming, and brocade work injures women's labor.

sentences.zh: 首創奢淫，危亡之漸。

translations.literal: To be first to create luxury and excess is the gradual onset of peril and ruin.
translations.idiomatic: To be the first to indulge in luxury and excess is the first step toward ruin.

sentences.zh: 漆器不已，必金為之；

translations.literal: If lacquer vessels do not cease, they must be made of gold;
translations.idiomatic: If lacquer vessels are not enough, vessels will be made of gold;

sentences.zh: 金器不已，必玉為之。

translations.literal: if gold vessels do not cease, they must be made of jade.
translations.idiomatic: if gold is not enough, they will be made of jade.

sentences.zh: 所以諍臣必諫其漸，及其滿盈，無所復諫。

translations.literal: Therefore remonstrating ministers must remonstrate at the gradual stage; when it is full and overflowing, there is nothing left to remonstrate about.
translations.idiomatic: That is why remonstrating ministers must speak at the first sign of excess. Once luxury has run its course, there is nothing left to remonstrate about.

sentences.zh: 」太宗以為然，因曰：「夫為人君，不憂萬姓而事奢淫，危亡之機可反掌而待也。

translations.literal: " Taizong considered this correct and said: "For one who is lord of men, not to worry for the myriad people but to pursue luxury and excess—the moment of peril and ruin may be awaited with a turn of the hand.
translations.idiomatic: " Taizong agreed and added, "For a ruler to neglect the people and pursue luxury and excess is to invite ruin in the blink of an eye.

sentences.zh: 」時皇子年幼者多任都督、刺史，遂良上疏曰：「昔兩漢以郡國理人，除郡以外，分立諸子。

translations.literal: " At the time many young princes were appointed area commanders and prefects; Suiliang submitted a memorial saying: "Formerly the two Han used commanderies and kingdoms to govern the people; apart from commanderies they established the sons separately.
translations.idiomatic: " At that time many young princes were appointed area commanders and prefects. Suiliang submitted a memorial: "In the two Han dynasties the realm was governed through commanderies and kingdoms, and apart from the commanderies the sons were granted separate domains.

sentences.zh: 割土分疆，雜用周制。

translations.literal: They carved territory and divided borders, mixing in Zhou institutions.
translations.idiomatic: Territory was carved up and borders divided, mixing Zhou institutions into the system.

sentences.zh: 皇唐州縣，祖依秦法。

translations.literal: Great Tang's prefectures and counties follow the Qin law in origin.
translations.idiomatic: Our Tang prefectures and counties follow the Qin model in origin.

sentences.zh: 皇子幼年，或授刺史，陛下豈不以王之骨肉，鎮扞四方？

translations.literal: When princes are young they are sometimes made prefects—does Your Majesty not intend, with the king's own flesh and bone, to guard and defend the four quarters?
translations.idiomatic: When princes are still young they are sometimes made prefects. Does Your Majesty not intend, by placing your own flesh and blood in office, to guard the four quarters?

sentences.zh: 此之造制，道高前烈。

translations.literal: This institution in its making—the Way surpasses former worthies.
translations.idiomatic: In establishing this policy Your Majesty has surpassed the former sages.

sentences.zh: 如臣愚見，有小未盡。

translations.literal: In this humble subject's foolish view, there is a small matter not yet fully achieved.
translations.idiomatic: In my humble view, one small point has not yet been fully realized.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: What is it?
translations.idiomatic: What is it?

sentences.zh: 刺史郡帥，民仰以安。

translations.literal: Prefects are the commanders of commanderies; the people rely on them for peace.
translations.idiomatic: Prefects are the leaders of their commanderies, and the people depend on them for security.

sentences.zh: 得一善人，部內蘇息；

translations.literal: Obtain one good man and the district revives;
translations.idiomatic: With one good man in office the district revives;

sentences.zh: 遇一不善，合州勞弊。

translations.literal: meet one who is not good and the whole prefecture is worn and exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: with one bad man the whole prefecture is worn down and exhausted.

sentences.zh: 是以人君愛恤百姓，常為擇賢。

translations.literal: Therefore the lord of men, loving and caring for the hundred surnames, constantly selects the worthy for them.
translations.idiomatic: That is why a ruler who loves his people constantly chooses worthy men for office.

sentences.zh: 或稱河潤九里，京師蒙福；

translations.literal: Some say the river moistens for nine li and the capital receives blessing;
translations.idiomatic: Some say that when a river nourishes the land for nine li, the capital itself shares in the blessing;

sentences.zh: 或人興歌詠，生為立祠。

translations.literal: or the people rise in song and praise and erect shrines while he still lives.
translations.idiomatic: or the people break into song and erect shrines to a living official while he still serves.

sentences.zh: 漢宣帝云：『與我共理者，惟良二千石。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuan of Han said: 'Those who govern with me are only good two-thousand-bushel officials.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan of Han said, 'Those who govern with me are only good prefects.

sentences.zh: 』如臣愚見，陛下兒子內年齒尚幼、未堪臨人者，且留京師，教以經學。

translations.literal: ' In this humble subject's foolish view, among Your Majesty's sons those still young in years and not yet fit to oversee people should for the present remain in the capital and be taught the classics.
translations.idiomatic: ' In my humble view, among Your Majesty's sons those who are still young and not yet fit to govern people should remain in the capital for the present and be instructed in the classics.

sentences.zh: 一則畏天之威，不敢犯禁；

translations.literal: First, they will fear Heaven's majesty and not dare violate prohibitions;
translations.idiomatic: First, they will fear Heaven's majesty and not dare break the law;

sentences.zh: 二則觀見朝儀，自然成立。

translations.literal: second, observing court ritual they will naturally take form.
translations.idiomatic: second, by observing court ritual they will naturally learn how to conduct themselves.

sentences.zh: 因此積習，自知為人。

translations.literal: Through such accumulated practice they will themselves know how to be men.
translations.idiomatic: Through such long practice they will learn on their own how to be proper men.

sentences.zh: 審堪臨州，然後遣出。

translations.literal: When it is verified that they can oversee a prefecture, then send them out.
translations.idiomatic: Only when they are truly fit to govern a prefecture should they be sent out.

sentences.zh: 臣謹按漢明、章、和三帝，能友愛於弟，自茲已降，取為準的。

translations.literal: This subject respectfully notes that the three emperors Ming, Zhang, and He of Han were able to show brotherly love to their younger brothers; from this time down, take them as the standard.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully note that Emperors Ming, Zhang, and He of Han were able to show brotherly love toward their younger brothers. From their reigns down, they should be taken as the standard.

sentences.zh: 封立諸王，雖各有國土，年尚幼小者，召留京師，訓以禮法，垂以恩惠。

translations.literal: When enfeoffing and establishing the princes, though each had his own territory, those still young in years were summoned to remain in the capital, instructed in ritual and law, and bestowed with grace.
translations.idiomatic: When they enfeoffed the princes, although each had his own domain, those who were still young were summoned to remain in the capital, instructed in ritual and law, and showered with favor.

sentences.zh: 訖三帝世，諸王數十百人，唯二王稍惡，自余餐和染教，皆為善人。

translations.literal: Through the three emperors' reigns the princes numbered in the tens and hundreds; only two princes were somewhat bad—the rest, nourished by harmony and dyed by instruction, all became good men.
translations.idiomatic: Through the reigns of those three emperors the princes numbered in the tens and hundreds. Only two princes turned out badly; the rest, nourished by harmony and shaped by instruction, all became good men.

sentences.zh: 則前事已驗，惟陛下詳察。

translations.literal: Thus the former matter has been verified—may Your Majesty examine it in detail.
translations.idiomatic: The precedent has already been proved. I beg Your Majesty to consider it carefully.

sentences.zh: 」太宗深納之。

translations.literal: " Taizong deeply accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: " Taizong accepted the advice wholeheartedly.

sentences.zh: 其年，太子承乾以罪廢，魏王泰入侍，太宗面許立為太子。

translations.literal: That year Crown Prince Chengqian was deposed for crime; the Prince of Wei Tai attended in attendance and Taizong to his face promised to establish him as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: That year Crown Prince Chengqian was deposed for his crimes. The Prince of Wei, Li Tai, attended the emperor in person, and Taizong openly promised to make him crown prince.

sentences.zh: 因謂侍臣曰：「昨青雀自投我懷云：『臣今日始得與陛下為子，更生之日也。

translations.literal: He then said to the attending ministers: "Yesterday Green Sparrow threw himself into my arms and said: 'Today I have at last become your son—this is the day of my rebirth.
translations.idiomatic: He then told his attending ministers, "Yesterday Green Sparrow threw himself into my arms and said, 'Today I have at last truly become your son. This is the day of my rebirth.

sentences.zh: 臣唯有一子，臣百年之後，當為陛下殺之，傳國晉王。

translations.literal: I have only one son; after my hundred years I will kill him for Your Majesty and pass the realm to the Prince of Jin.'
translations.idiomatic: I have only one son. After I die I will kill him for Your Majesty and pass the realm to the Prince of Jin.'

sentences.zh: 』父子之道，故當天性，我見其如此，甚憐之。

translations.literal: ' The way of father and son is naturally inborn feeling—I saw him thus and greatly pitied him.
translations.idiomatic: ' The bond between father and son is a matter of natural feeling. When I saw him speak this way, I was deeply moved.

sentences.zh: 」遂良進曰：「陛下失言。

translations.literal: " Suiliang advanced and said: "Your Majesty has misspoken.
translations.idiomatic: " Suiliang stepped forward and said, "Your Majesty has spoken unwisely.

sentences.zh: 伏願審思，無令錯誤也。

translations.literal: I bow and wish Your Majesty to consider carefully and not let error stand.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly beg Your Majesty to think this through carefully and not let a mistake stand.

sentences.zh: 安有陛下百年之後，魏王執權為天下之主，而能殺其愛子，傳國於晉王者乎？

translations.literal: How could there be, after Your Majesty's hundred years, the Prince of Wei holding power as lord of all under Heaven yet able to kill his beloved son and pass the realm to the Prince of Jin?
translations.idiomatic: After Your Majesty is gone, when the Prince of Wei holds power as ruler of the realm, how could he kill his own beloved son and pass the throne to the Prince of Jin?

sentences.zh: 陛下昔立承乾為太子，而復寵愛魏王，禮數或有逾於承乾者，良由嫡庶不分，所以至此。

translations.literal: Your Majesty formerly established Chengqian as crown prince yet again favored the Prince of Wei, ritual sometimes exceeding Chengqian's—truly because legitimate and secondary were not distinguished, hence arriving at this.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty once made Chengqian crown prince, yet you also favored the Prince of Wei, whose ceremonial treatment sometimes exceeded Chengqian's. This came about because the lines of legitimate and secondary sons were not kept distinct.

sentences.zh: 殷鑑不遠，足為龜鏡。

translations.literal: The mirror of Yin is not far—sufficient as a tortoise mirror.
translations.idiomatic: The lesson of the Yin dynasty is not far off and should serve as a clear warning.

sentences.zh: 陛下今日既立魏王，伏願陛下別安置晉王，始得安全耳。

translations.literal: Your Majesty today having established the Prince of Wei, I bow and wish Your Majesty separately to settle the Prince of Jin—only then can he be safe.
translations.idiomatic: Now that Your Majesty is about to make the Prince of Wei heir, I beg you to make separate arrangements for the Prince of Jin. Only then will he be safe.

sentences.zh: 」太宗涕泗交下曰：「我不能。

translations.literal: " Taizong's tears and mucus flowed together and he said: "I cannot.
translations.idiomatic: " Taizong wept openly and said, "I cannot do it.

sentences.zh: 」即日召長孫無忌、房玄齡、李勣與遂良等定策，立晉王為皇太子。

translations.literal: " That same day he summoned Zhangsun Wuji, Fang Xuanling, Li Ji, and Suiliang and others to fix the policy and established the Prince of Jin as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: " That same day he summoned Zhangsun Wuji, Fang Xuanling, Li Ji, Suiliang, and others to settle the succession and installed the Prince of Jin as crown prince.

sentences.zh: 時頻有飛雉集於宮殿之內，太宗問群臣曰：「是何祥也？

translations.literal: At the time pheasants in flight frequently gathered within the palace halls; Taizong asked the ministers: "What omen is this?
translations.idiomatic: At that time wild pheasants were frequently seen flying into the palace precincts. Taizong asked his ministers, "What omen does this portend?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「昔秦文公時，有童子化為雉，雌者鳴於陳倉，雄者鳴於南陽。

translations.literal: " They replied: "Formerly in the time of Duke Wen of Qin a boy transformed into a pheasant; the female cried at Chencang and the male at Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: " They replied, "In the time of Duke Wen of Qin a boy was transformed into a pheasant. The female cried at Chencang and the male at Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 童子曰：得雄者王，得雌者霸。

translations.literal: The boy said: He who obtains the male will be king; he who obtains the female will be hegemon.
translations.idiomatic: The boy said, 'He who obtains the male will become king; he who obtains the female will become hegemon.'

sentences.zh: 文公遂以為寶雞。

translations.literal: Duke Wen thereupon took it as the treasured cock.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Wen thereupon took this as the omen of the treasured cock.

sentences.zh: 後漢光武得雄，遂起南陽而有四海。

translations.literal: Later Emperor Guangwu of Han obtained the male and thereupon rose from Nanyang to possess the four seas.
translations.idiomatic: Later Emperor Guangwu of Han obtained the male bird, rose from Nanyang, and won the realm.

sentences.zh: 陛下舊封秦王，故雄雉見於秦地，此所以彰表明德也。

translations.literal: Your Majesty was formerly enfeoffed as Prince of Qin; therefore the male pheasant appears in Qin territory—this is how bright virtue is made manifest.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty was once Prince of Qin, so the male pheasant appears in Qin territory. This is how your bright virtue is made manifest.

sentences.zh: 」太宗悅曰：「立身之道，不可無學，遂良博識，深可重也。

translations.literal: " Taizong was pleased and said: "The way of establishing oneself cannot be without learning—Suiliang is broadly learned and deeply to be valued.
translations.idiomatic: " Taizong was pleased and said, "One cannot establish oneself without learning. Suiliang is broadly learned and deserves great respect.

sentences.zh: 」尋授太子賓客。

translations.literal: " Shortly he was appointed Mentor of the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: " Soon afterward he was appointed mentor of the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 時薛延陀遣使請婚，太宗許以女妻之，納其財聘，既而不與。

translations.literal: At the time Xueyantuo sent envoys requesting marriage; Taizong promised a daughter as wife, accepted their bride-price gifts, yet afterward did not give her.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Xueyantuo sent envoys to request a marriage alliance. Taizong promised them a princess, accepted their bride-price gifts, and then refused to give her.

sentences.zh: 遂良上疏曰：

translations.literal: Suiliang submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Suiliang submitted a memorial:

sentences.zh: 時太宗欲親征高麗，顧謂侍臣曰：「高麗莫離支賊殺其王，虐用其人。

translations.literal: At the time Taizong wished to campaign in person against Goguryeo and, turning to the attending ministers, said: "Goguryeo's Yeon Gaesomun treacherously killed his king and cruelly abused his people.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Taizong wished to campaign in person against Goguryeo. Turning to his attending ministers he said, "Yeon Gaesomun of Goguryeo murdered his king and cruelly abused his people.

sentences.zh: 夫出師吊伐，當乘機便，今因其弒虐，誅之甚易。

translations.literal: To send forth the army on a punitive expedition should seize opportune moments—now, taking advantage of his regicide and cruelty, executing him would be very easy.
translations.idiomatic: To send an army on a punitive expedition one must seize the right moment. Now, with his regicide and cruelty as our cause, destroying him would be very easy.

sentences.zh: 」遂良對曰：「陛下兵機神算，人莫能知。

translations.literal: " Suiliang replied: "Your Majesty's military stratagems and divine calculations—no one can know them.
translations.idiomatic: " Suiliang replied, "Your Majesty's military stratagems and divine calculations are beyond anyone's knowledge.

sentences.zh: 昔隋末亂離，手平寇亂。

translations.literal: Formerly at the end of Sui there was disorder and separation; with your own hand you pacified rebel chaos.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Sui you yourself pacified the rebel chaos.

sentences.zh: 及北狄侵邊，西蕃失禮，陛下欲命將擊之，群臣莫不苦諫，陛下獨斷進討，卒並誅夷。

translations.literal: When the northern Di invaded the borders and the western tribes lost propriety, Your Majesty wished to order generals to strike them; the ministers all earnestly remonstrated, yet Your Majesty alone decided to advance and attack, and in the end all were executed and exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: When the northern barbarians invaded the frontier and the western tribes showed disrespect, Your Majesty wished to send generals against them. All the ministers remonstrated strenuously, yet Your Majesty decided alone to advance, and in the end they were all destroyed.

sentences.zh: 海內之人，徼外之國，畏威懾伏，為此舉也。

translations.literal: The people within the seas and the states beyond the frontiers feared your majesty and submitted in awe—it was for this action.
translations.idiomatic: The people within the seas and the states beyond the frontiers feared your majesty and submitted. It was because of such actions.

sentences.zh: 今陛下將興師遼東，臣意熒惑。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty will raise the army in Liaodong—this subject's mind is confused and doubtful.
translations.idiomatic: Now that Your Majesty is about to raise an army in Liaodong, I am deeply troubled.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 陛下神武，不比前代人君。

translations.literal: Your Majesty is divinely martial, not comparable to rulers of former generations.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is divinely martial and not to be compared with rulers of former ages.

sentences.zh: 兵既渡遼，指期克捷，萬一差跌，無以威示遠方，若再發忿兵，則安危難測。

translations.literal: Once the army has crossed the Liao, victory is expected on schedule; if by any chance there is a slip, there will be no way to display majesty to distant regions—if angry troops are sent forth again, then security and peril cannot be measured.
translations.idiomatic: Once the army has crossed the Liao, victory is expected on schedule. But if anything goes wrong, you will have no way to display your majesty to distant lands. If you must send angry troops again, the outcome for the state cannot be foreseen.

sentences.zh: 」太宗深然之。

translations.literal: " Taizong deeply approved.
translations.idiomatic: " Taizong was deeply persuaded.

sentences.zh: 兵部尚書李勣曰：「近者延陀犯邊，陛下必欲追擊，此時陛下取魏徵之言，遂失機會。

translations.literal: Minister of War Li Ji said: "Recently when the Tiele violated the borders, Your Majesty wished to pursue and strike; at that time Your Majesty took Wei Zheng's words and thus lost the opportunity.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of War Li Ji said, "When the Tiele recently violated the frontier, Your Majesty wished to pursue them, but at that time you followed Wei Zheng's advice and lost the opportunity.

sentences.zh: 若如聖策，延陀無一人生還，可五十年間疆場無事。

translations.literal: If it had followed Your sage strategy, not one man of the Tiele would have returned alive and the borders could have been untroubled for fifty years.
translations.idiomatic: Had Your Majesty's plan been followed, not one Tiele man would have returned alive, and the frontier could have been peaceful for fifty years.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「誠如卿言，由魏徵誤計耳。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "Truly as you say—it was because Wei Zheng's plan was wrong.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "What you say is true. It was Wei Zheng's mistaken counsel.

sentences.zh: 朕不欲以一計不當而尤之，後有良算，安肯矢謀。

translations.literal: I do not wish to blame him for one plan not fitting; if later there is a good plan, how would I abandon counsel?
translations.idiomatic: I do not wish to blame him for one mistaken plan. If he offers good counsel in future, how could I refuse to heed it?

sentences.zh: 」由是從勣之言，經畫渡遼之師。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he followed Ji's words and planned the army to cross the Liao.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon he followed Li Ji's advice and planned the campaign to cross the Liao.

sentences.zh: 遂良以太宗銳意三韓，懼其遺悔，翌日上疏諫曰：

translations.literal: Suiliang, because Taizong was keen on the Three Han, feared he would leave regret; the next day he submitted a memorial remonstrating:
translations.idiomatic: Because Taizong was set on the Three Han kingdoms, Suiliang feared the emperor would later regret the decision. The next day he submitted a remonstrance memorial:

sentences.zh: 太宗不納。

translations.literal: Taizong did not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong did not accept his advice.

sentences.zh: 十八年，拜黃門侍郎，參綜朝政。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was appointed Vice Director of the Yellow Gate and participated in comprehensive court governance.
translations.idiomatic: In 644 he was appointed vice director of the Yellow Gate and took part in governing the court.

sentences.zh: 高麗莫離支遣使貢白金，遂良言於太宗曰：「莫離支虐弒其主，九夷所不容，陛下以之興兵，將事吊伐，為遼山之人報主辱之恥。

translations.literal: Goguryeo's Yeon Gaesomun sent envoys offering tribute of white gold; Suiliang said to Taizong: "Yeon Gaesomun cruelly murdered his lord—the nine Yi cannot tolerate him. Your Majesty raises the army to undertake a punitive expedition and avenge for the people of Liaoshan the shame done their lord.
translations.idiomatic: Yeon Gaesomun of Goguryeo sent envoys offering tribute of white gold. Suiliang said to Taizong, "Yeon Gaesomun cruelly murdered his sovereign, an act intolerable among the eastern peoples. Your Majesty is raising an army to punish him and avenge for the people of Liaodong the shame done their lord.

sentences.zh: 古者，討弒君之賊，不受其賂。

translations.literal: In antiquity, when punishing regicides, one did not accept their bribes.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity, when punishing regicides, one did not accept their bribes.

sentences.zh: 昔宋督遺魯君以郜鼎，桓公受之於太廟，臧哀伯諫曰：『君人者昭德塞違，今滅德立違，而置其賂器於太廟，百官象之，其又何誅焉？

translations.literal: Formerly Minister Du of Song presented the Duke of Lu with the tripod of Zou; Duke Huan received it in the Grand Temple. Zang Aibo remonstrated: 'The lord of men should display virtue and block wrongdoing; now you extinguish virtue and establish wrongdoing, yet place his bribe-vessel in the Grand Temple—the hundred officials will take it as a model—how then can wrong be punished?
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Minister Du of Song presented the tripod of Zou to the Duke of Lu, and Duke Huan received it in the Grand Temple. Zang Aibo remonstrated, 'A ruler should display virtue and block wrongdoing. Now you extinguish virtue and establish wrongdoing, yet place his bribe in the Grand Temple. When the hundred officials take this as their model, how can wrongdoing be punished?

sentences.zh: 武王克商，遷九鼎於洛邑，義士猶或非之，而況將昭違亂之賂器，置諸太廟，其若之何？

translations.literal: King Wu conquered Shang and moved the nine tripods to Luoyi—men of righteousness still criticized this; how much more to display the bribe-vessel of rebellion and disorder and place it in the Grand Temple—what is to be done?
translations.idiomatic: When King Wu conquered Shang and moved the nine tripods to Luoyi, men of righteousness still criticized him. How much more objectionable is it to display the bribe of a rebel and place it in the Grand Temple?

sentences.zh: 』夫《春秋》之書，百王取法，若受不臣之筐篚，納弒逆之朝貢，不以為愆，何所致伐？

translations.literal: ' The book Spring and Autumn is the law taken by a hundred kings. If one accepts the baskets of an unsubmissive man and receives the court tribute of a regicide, and does not regard it as fault—on what grounds can one launch punitive attack?
translations.idiomatic: ' The Spring and Autumn Annals is the standard for a hundred kings. If you accept gifts from an unsubmissive man and receive tribute from a regicide without regarding it as fault, on what grounds can you launch a punitive expedition?

sentences.zh: 臣謂莫離支所獻，自不得受。

translations.literal: This subject holds that what Yeon Gaesomun offers naturally may not be received.
translations.idiomatic: I hold that what Yeon Gaesomun offers must not be accepted.

sentences.zh: 」太宗納焉，以其使屬吏。

translations.literal: " Taizong accepted this and handed his envoys over to the officials.
translations.idiomatic: " Taizong accepted this advice and handed the envoys over to the officials for punishment.

sentences.zh: 太宗既滅高昌，每歲調發千餘人防遏其地，遂良上疏曰：

translations.literal: After Taizong had destroyed Gaochang, each year more than a thousand men were levied to guard and block that territory; Suiliang submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: After Taizong destroyed Gaochang, more than a thousand men were levied each year to garrison the region. Suiliang submitted a memorial:

sentences.zh: 二十年，太宗於寢殿側別置一院，令太子居，絕不令往東宮。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year Taizong separately established a courtyard beside the sleeping hall and ordered the crown prince to dwell there, absolutely not allowing him to go to the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In 646 Taizong set up a separate courtyard beside his sleeping quarters for the crown prince to live in and absolutely forbade him to go to the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 遂良復上疏諫曰：

translations.literal: Suiliang again submitted a memorial remonstrating:
translations.idiomatic: Suiliang again submitted a remonstrance memorial:

sentences.zh: 太宗從之。

translations.literal: Taizong followed it.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong accepted his advice.

sentences.zh: 遂良前後諫奏及陳便宜書數十上，多見採納，其年，加銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Suiliang before and after submitted remonstrances and memorials on practical measures numbering in the tens; many were adopted. That year he was made Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Silver Seal.
translations.idiomatic: Suiliang submitted dozens of remonstrances and practical proposals, many of which were adopted. That year he was promoted to grand master of splendid happiness with silver seal.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，以本官檢校大理卿，尋丁父憂解。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year, with his present office he was made acting Chief of the Court of Judicial Review; shortly he resigned on mourning for his father.
translations.idiomatic: In 647 he was made acting chief of the Court of Judicial Review while retaining his present office. Soon afterward he resigned to observe mourning for his father.

sentences.zh: 明年，起復舊職，俄拜中書令。

translations.literal: The next year he was recalled to his former post and shortly was appointed Chief of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was recalled to his former post and soon appointed chief of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，太宗寢疾，召遂良及長孫無忌入臥內，謂之曰：「卿等忠烈，簡在朕心。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year Taizong lay ill; he summoned Suiliang and Zhangsun Wuji into his sleeping quarters and said to them: "You are loyal and steadfast—selected and kept in my heart.
translations.idiomatic: In 649 Taizong fell gravely ill. He summoned Suiliang and Zhangsun Wuji to his bedside and said, "Your loyalty and steadfastness are engraved in my heart.

sentences.zh: 昔漢武寄霍光，劉備托葛亮，朕之後事，一以委卿。

translations.literal: Formerly Emperor Wu of Han entrusted Huo Guang; Liu Bei entrusted Zhuge Liang—my later affairs I wholly entrust to you.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Han entrusted Huo Guang, and Liu Bei entrusted Zhuge Liang. I entrust all my affairs after death to you.

sentences.zh: 太子仁孝，卿之所悉，必須盡誠輔佐，永保宗社。

translations.literal: The crown prince is benevolent and filial—as you know—you must with full sincerity assist him and forever preserve the altars of state.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince is benevolent and filial, as you know. You must assist him with full sincerity and preserve the altars of state forever.

sentences.zh: 」又顧謂太子曰：「無忌、遂良在，國家之事，汝無憂矣。

translations.literal: " He again turned and said to the crown prince: "With Wuji and Suiliang present, in matters of state you need not worry.
translations.idiomatic: " He then turned to the crown prince and said, "With Wuji and Suiliang at your side, you need not worry about the affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 」仍命遂良草詔。

translations.literal: " He still ordered Suiliang to draft the edict.
translations.idiomatic: " He also ordered Suiliang to draft his final edict.

sentences.zh: 高宗即位，賜爵河南縣公。

translations.literal: When Gaozong took the throne he was granted the title Marquis of Henan County.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozong took the throne, Suiliang was granted the title Marquis of Henan County.

sentences.zh: 永徽元年，進封郡公。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yonghui he was advanced to Duke of a commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In 650 he was promoted to duke of a commandery.

sentences.zh: 尋坐事出為同州刺史。

translations.literal: Shortly, on account of an affair, he was sent out as prefect of Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, because of an affair, he was sent out as prefect of Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 三年，征拜吏部尚書、同中書門下三品，監修國史，加光祿大夫。

translations.literal: In the third year he was summoned and appointed Minister of Personnel, with the same third rank as Secretariat-Chancellery, supervising compilation of the national history, and made Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: In 652 he was recalled and appointed minister of personnel with third rank at the Secretariat-Chancellery, put in charge of compiling the national history, and made grand master for splendid happiness.

sentences.zh: 其月，又兼太子賓客。

translations.literal: That same month he also served concurrently as Mentor of the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: That same month he also served concurrently as mentor of the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 四年，代張行成為尚書右僕射，依舊知政事。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he replaced Zhang Xingcheng as Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, still managing court affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In 653 he replaced Zhang Xingcheng as right vice director of the Department of State Affairs and continued to manage court affairs.

sentences.zh: 六年，高宗將廢皇后王氏，立昭儀武氏為皇后，召太尉長孫無忌、司空李勣、尚書左僕射於志寧及遂良以籌其事。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Gaozong was about to depose Empress Wang and establish Lady Wu of the Bright Countenance as empress; he summoned Grand Mentor Zhangsun Wuji, Minister of Works Li Ji, Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs Yu Zhining, and Suiliang to deliberate the matter.
translations.idiomatic: In 655 Gaozong was about to depose Empress Wang and make Lady Wu empress. He summoned Grand Mentor Zhangsun Wuji, Minister of Works Li Ji, Left Vice Director Yu Zhining, and Suiliang to deliberate the matter.

sentences.zh: 將入，遂良謂無忌等曰：「上意欲廢中宮，必議其事，遂良今欲陳諫，眾意如何？

translations.literal: As they were about to enter, Suiliang said to Wuji and the others: "The sovereign's intent is to depose the central palace—he will surely discuss the matter. Suiliang now wishes to remonstrate—what is the group's intent?
translations.idiomatic: Before they entered, Suiliang said to Wuji and the others, "The emperor intends to depose the empress and will surely raise the matter. I mean to remonstrate. What do you think?

sentences.zh: 」無忌曰：「明公必須極言，無忌請繼焉。

translations.literal: " Wuji said: "Your Excellency must speak to the utmost—I, Wuji, ask to follow after.
translations.idiomatic: " Wuji said, "You must speak with full force. I will follow after you.

sentences.zh: 」及入，高宗難於發言，再三顧謂無忌曰：「莫大之罪，絕嗣為甚。

translations.literal: " When they entered, Gaozong found it hard to speak; again and again he turned and said to Wuji: "Of great crimes, having no heir is the gravest.
translations.idiomatic: " When they entered, Gaozong found it hard to speak. Again and again he turned to Wuji and said, "Of great crimes, having no heir is the gravest.

sentences.zh: 皇后無胤息，昭儀有子，今欲立為皇后，公等以為何如？

translations.literal: The empress has no offspring; the Bright Countenance has a son. I now wish to establish her as empress—what do you gentlemen think?
translations.idiomatic: The empress has no children, but Lady Wu has a son. I now wish to make her empress. What do you think?

sentences.zh: 」遂良曰：「皇后出自名家，先朝所娶，伏事先帝，無愆婦德。

translations.literal: " Suiliang said: "The empress comes from an eminent house; the former court married her. She served the late emperor without fault in wifely virtue.
translations.idiomatic: " Suiliang said, "The empress comes from an eminent family and was married by the former emperor. She served the late emperor without fault in wifely conduct.

sentences.zh: 先帝不豫，執陛下手以語臣曰：『我好兒好婦，今將付卿。

translations.literal: When the late emperor was ill he took Your Majesty's hand and said to me: 'I have a good son and a good daughter-in-law; I now entrust them to you.
translations.idiomatic: When the late emperor was ill he took Your Majesty's hand and said to me, 'I have a good son and a good daughter-in-law. I now entrust them to you.

sentences.zh: 』陛下親承德音，言猶在耳。

translations.literal: ' Your Majesty personally received this virtuous charge—the words are still in the ear.
translations.idiomatic: ' Your Majesty received this charge in person. His words are still in our ears.

sentences.zh: 皇后自此未聞有愆，恐不可廢。

translations.literal: Since then no fault has been heard of the empress—I fear she may not be deposed.
translations.idiomatic: Since then no fault has been heard against the empress. I fear she cannot be deposed.

sentences.zh: 臣今不敢曲從，上違先帝之命，特願再三思審。

translations.literal: This subject now dares not bend to comply, going above against the late emperor's command—I especially wish Your Majesty to think and examine again and again.
translations.idiomatic: I dare not bend to comply and violate the late emperor's command. I beg Your Majesty to think this through again and again.

sentences.zh: 愚臣上忤聖顏，罪合萬死，但願不負先朝厚恩，何顧性命？

translations.literal: This foolish subject above offends the sage countenance—my crime deserves ten thousand deaths; I only wish not to fail the former court's deep grace—what care for life?
translations.idiomatic: In offending Your Majesty I deserve death ten thousand times over, but I wish only not to fail the deep grace of the former court. What care I for my life?

sentences.zh: 」遂良致笏於殿陛，曰：「還陛下此笏。

translations.literal: " Suiliang placed his tablet on the hall steps and said: "I return to Your Majesty this tablet.
translations.idiomatic: " Suiliang placed his court tablet on the hall steps and said, "I return this tablet to Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 」仍解巾叩頭流血。

translations.literal: " He also removed his headcloth and knocked his head until blood flowed.
translations.idiomatic: " He removed his headcloth and knocked his head on the floor until blood flowed.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，令引出。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly angered and ordered him led out.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and ordered him led out.

sentences.zh: 長孫無忌曰：「遂良受先朝顧命，有罪不加刑。

translations.literal: Zhangsun Wuji said: "Suiliang received the former court's deathbed charge—for crime no punishment should be added.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangsun Wuji said, "Suiliang received the late emperor's deathbed charge. Even if he has offended, he should not be punished.

sentences.zh: 」翌日，帝謂李勣曰：「冊立武昭儀之事，遂良固執不從。

translations.literal: " The next day the emperor said to Li Ji: "On the matter of enfeoffing Lady Wu as empress, Suiliang stubbornly would not comply.
translations.idiomatic: " The next day the emperor said to Li Ji, "On the matter of making Lady Wu empress, Suiliang stubbornly refused to comply.

sentences.zh: 遂良既是受顧命大臣，事若不可，當且止也。

translations.literal: Since Suiliang is a minister who received the deathbed charge, if the matter cannot be done, it should for the present be stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Since Suiliang is a minister who received the deathbed charge, if the matter cannot be done, it should be stopped for now.

sentences.zh: 」勣對曰：「此乃陛下家事，不合問外人。

translations.literal: " Ji replied: "This is Your Majesty's family affair—it is not fitting to ask outsiders.
translations.idiomatic: " Li Ji replied, "This is Your Majesty's family affair. It is not fitting to ask outsiders.

sentences.zh: 」帝乃立昭儀為皇后，左遷遂良潭州都督。

translations.literal: " The emperor thereupon established the Bright Countenance as empress and demoted Suiliang to area commander of Tanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor thereupon made Lady Wu empress and demoted Suiliang to area commander of Tanzhou.

sentences.zh: 顯慶二年，轉桂州都督。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianqing he was transferred to area commander of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In 657 he was transferred to area commander of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 未幾，又貶為愛州刺史。

translations.literal: Before long he was again demoted to prefect of Aizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was demoted again to prefect of Aizhou.

sentences.zh: 明年，卒官，年六十三。

translations.literal: The next year he died in office, aged sixty-three.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he died in office at the age of sixty-three.

sentences.zh: 遂良卒後二歲餘，許敬宗、李義府奏言長孫無忌所構逆謀，並遂良搧動，乃追削官爵，子孫配流愛州。

translations.literal: More than two years after Suiliang's death, Xu Jingzong and Li Yifu memorialized that Zhangsun Wuji had plotted rebellion and that Suiliang had incited it; his offices and titles were then posthumously stripped and his descendants were banished to Aizhou.
translations.idiomatic: More than two years after Suiliang's death, Xu Jingzong and Li Yifu memorialized that Zhangsun Wuji had plotted rebellion and that Suiliang had incited him. Suiliang's offices and titles were posthumously stripped, and his descendants were banished to Aizhou.

sentences.zh: 弘道元年二月，高宗遺詔放還本郡。

translations.literal: In the second month of the first year of Hongdao, Gaozong's deathbed edict ordered them returned to their native commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of 683, Gaozong's deathbed edict ordered them returned to their native commandery.

sentences.zh: 神龍元年，則天遺制復遂良及韓瑗爵位。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shenlong, Empress Wu's deathbed decree restored the titles of Suiliang and Han Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: In 705, Empress Wu's deathbed decree restored the titles of Suiliang and Han Yuan.

sentences.zh: =韓瑗=

translations.literal: =Han Yuan=
translations.idiomatic: Han Yuan

sentences.zh: 韓瑗，雍州三原人也。

translations.literal: Han Yuan was a man of Sanyuan in Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Han Yuan was a native of Sanyuan in Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 祖紹，隋太僕少卿。

translations.literal: His grandfather Shao was Vice Director of the Imperial Stud in Sui.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Shao served as vice director of the imperial stud under the Sui.

sentences.zh: 父仲良，武德初為大理少卿，受詔與郎楚之等掌定律令。

translations.literal: His father Zhongliang, at the beginning of Wude, was Vice Chief of the Court of Judicial Review and received an edict with Lang Chuzhi and others to oversee fixing the statutes and ordinances.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhongliang, at the beginning of the Wude era, served as vice chief of the Court of Judicial Review and was ordered with Lang Chuzhi and others to oversee the codification of law.

sentences.zh: 仲良言於高祖曰：「周代之律，其屬三千，秦法已來，約為五百。

translations.literal: Zhongliang said to Gaozu: "The laws of the Zhou had three thousand articles; since Qin law there have been about five hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongliang said to Emperor Gaozu, "The laws of the Zhou had three thousand articles, but since the Qin there have been about five hundred.

sentences.zh: 若遠依周制，繁紊更多。

translations.literal: If we far follow Zhou institutions, complexity and disorder will be even greater.
translations.idiomatic: If we follow the Zhou model closely, the laws will become even more complex.

sentences.zh: 且官吏至公，自當奉法，苟若徇己，豈顧刑名？

translations.literal: Moreover, if officials are utterly fair they will naturally uphold the law; if they indulge themselves, will they care for penal names?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, if officials are truly impartial they will uphold the law of their own accord. If they indulge themselves, what care have they for the statutes?

sentences.zh: 請崇寬簡，以允惟新之望。

translations.literal: I ask that leniency and simplicity be honored to fulfill the hope of renewal.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that leniency and simplicity be honored to fulfill the hope of a new beginning.

sentences.zh: 」高祖然之。

translations.literal: " Gaozu approved.
translations.idiomatic: " Emperor Gaozu approved.

sentences.zh: 於是采定《開皇律》行之，時以為便。

translations.literal: Thereupon they adopted and fixed the Kaihuang Code to put it in practice; at the time it was considered convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon they adopted the Kaihuang Code and put it into practice, and at the time it was considered convenient.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，位至刑部尚書、秦州都督府長史、潁川縣公。

translations.literal: In Zhenguan he reached Minister of Punishments, Chief Administrator of the Qinzhou Area Command, and Duke of Yingchuan County.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenguan era he rose to minister of punishments, chief administrator of the Qinzhou area command, and Duke of Yingchuan County.

sentences.zh: 瑗少有節操，博學有吏才。

translations.literal: Yuan from youth had integrity, was broadly learned and had talent for administration.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Yuan had integrity, was broadly learned, and had talent for administration.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，累至兵部侍郎，襲父潁川公。

translations.literal: In Zhenguan he rose in succession to Vice Minister of War and inherited his father's title Duke of Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenguan era he rose to vice minister of war and inherited his father's title as Duke of Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 永徽三年，拜黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yonghui he was appointed Vice Director of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: In 652 he was appointed vice director of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 四年，與中書侍郎來濟皆同中書門下三品，監修國史。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he and Vice Director of the Secretariat Lai Ji were both given the same third rank at Secretariat-Chancellery and supervised compilation of the national history.
translations.idiomatic: In 653 he and Vice Director of the Secretariat Lai Ji were both given third rank at the Secretariat-Chancellery and put in charge of compiling the national history.

sentences.zh: 五年，加銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was made Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Silver Seal.
translations.idiomatic: In 654 he was made grand master of splendid happiness with silver seal.

sentences.zh: 六年，遷侍中，其年兼太子賓客。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was moved to Palace Attendant; that year he also served concurrently as Mentor of the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: In 655 he was promoted to palace attendant and that year also served concurrently as mentor of the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 時高宗欲廢王皇后，瑗涕泣諫曰：「皇后是陛下在籓府時先帝所娶，今無愆過，欲行廢黜，四海之士，誰不惕然？

translations.literal: At the time Gaozong wished to depose Empress Wang; Yuan wept and remonstrated: "The empress was married by the late emperor when Your Majesty was in the princely residence; now she has no fault—if you wish to carry out deposition, which man within the four seas will not be alarmed?
translations.idiomatic: At that time Gaozong wished to depose Empress Wang. Yuan wept as he remonstrated, "The empress was married to Your Majesty by the late emperor when you were still prince. She has committed no fault. If you depose her, who throughout the realm will not be alarmed?

sentences.zh: 且國家屢有廢立，非長久之術。

translations.literal: Moreover, when the state repeatedly has deposition and establishment, it is not a long-lasting method.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, repeated depositions and installations of empresses are no policy for long-term stability.

sentences.zh: 願陛下為社稷大計，無以臣愚，不垂采察。

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty, for the great plan of the altars of soil and grain, not because of this subject's foolishness, to fail to bestow examination and adoption.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty, for the sake of the altars of state, not to dismiss my counsel because I am foolish.

sentences.zh: 」帝不納。

translations.literal: " The emperor did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor did not accept his advice.

sentences.zh: 明日，瑗又諫，悲泣不能自勝。

translations.literal: The next day Yuan again remonstrated, grieving and weeping beyond control of himself.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Yuan remonstrated again, weeping so bitterly he could not control himself.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，促令引出。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly angered and urgently ordered him led out.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and ordered him led out at once.

sentences.zh: 尋而尚書左僕射褚遂良以忤旨左授潭州都督，瑗復上疏理之曰：

translations.literal: Shortly the Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs Chu Suiliang, for opposing the intent, was demoted to area commander of Tanzhou; Yuan again submitted a memorial pleading on his behalf:
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Left Vice Director Chu Suiliang was demoted to area commander of Tanzhou for opposing the emperor's will. Yuan again submitted a memorial in his defense:

sentences.zh: 古之聖王，立諫鼓，設謗木，冀欲聞逆耳之言，甘苦口之議，發揚大化，裨益洪猷，垂令譽於將來，播休聲於不朽者也。

translations.literal: The sage kings of antiquity set up remonstrance drums and erected slander posts, hoping to hear words that grate on the ear and accept counsel bitter in the mouth, to extend great transformation, benefit vast plans, leave fine reputation to the future, and spread good fame to immortality.
translations.idiomatic: The sage kings of antiquity set up remonstrance drums and erected complaint posts, hoping to hear words that grate on the ear and accept counsel that tastes bitter in the mouth, so as to extend great transformation, benefit vast plans, leave a fine reputation to posterity, and spread good fame forever.

sentences.zh: 伏見詔書以褚遂良為潭州都督，臣夙夜思之，用增感激。

translations.literal: I bow and have seen the edict appointing Chu Suiliang area commander of Tanzhou; day and night I have thought on it and thereby increased my deep emotion.
translations.idiomatic: I have seen the edict appointing Chu Suiliang area commander of Tanzhou. Day and night I have pondered it, and my distress has only grown.

sentences.zh: 臣識慚知遠，業謝通經，載撫愚情，誠為未可。

translations.literal: This subject's knowledge is ashamed before far sight; my accomplishment falls short of mastering the classics—bearing my foolish feelings, truly it should not be so.
translations.idiomatic: My knowledge is limited and my learning falls short of mastery of the classics, yet as I consider this in my foolish heart, I cannot believe it right.

sentences.zh: 遂良運偶昇平，道昭前烈，束髮從宦，方淹累稔。

translations.literal: Suiliang's fate met peaceful ascent; his Way illumined former worthies. From tying the hair he followed office, already submerged for many years.
translations.idiomatic: Suiliang's fate met an age of peace, and his conduct illumined the former sages. From youth he entered office and has served for many years.

sentences.zh: 趨侍陛下，俄歷歲年，不聞涓滴之愆，常睹勤勞之效。

translations.literal: Hastening to attend Your Majesty, soon years have passed—no drop of fault has been heard; I constantly see the effect of diligent toil.
translations.idiomatic: In attending Your Majesty he has already passed many years. Not a drop of fault has been heard against him, and his diligent service has constantly been seen.

sentences.zh: 竭忠誠於早歲，罄直道於茲年。

translations.literal: He exhausted loyalty in early years and spent the straight Way in these years.
translations.idiomatic: He exhausted his loyalty in his early years and has spent the straight path in these later years.

sentences.zh: 體國忘家，捐身徇物，風霜其操，鐵石其心。

translations.literal: Embodying the state and forgetting the family, he gave his person and followed the task; wind and frost are his conduct, iron and stone his heart.
translations.idiomatic: He has embodied the state and forgotten his family, given his person to public duty. His conduct is as firm as wind and frost, his heart as hard as iron and stone.

sentences.zh: 誠可重於皇明，詎專方於曩昔？

translations.literal: Truly he may be valued in the imperial brightness—how could he be valued only in former times?
translations.idiomatic: He deserves to be valued in the present reign. How could his worth belong only to former times?

sentences.zh: 且先帝納之於帷幄，寄之以心膂，德逾水石，義冠舟車，公家之利，言無不可。

translations.literal: Moreover the late emperor took him into the curtain and tent, entrusted him with heart and backbone; his virtue exceeded water and stone, his righteousness crowned boat and carriage—for the public family's benefit, in speech nothing was not permissible.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the late emperor took him into his inner council and entrusted him with his deepest trust. His virtue exceeded water and stone, his righteousness surpassed all others. For the benefit of the state, nothing he said was unacceptable.

sentences.zh: 及纏悲四海，遏密八音，竭忠國家，親承顧托，一德無二，千古懍然。

translations.literal: When grief enveloped the four seas and the eight tones were stilled, he exhausted loyalty for the state, personally received the deathbed entrustment—one virtue without a second, for a thousand ages awe-inspiring.
translations.idiomatic: When grief enveloped the realm and music was stilled, he exhausted his loyalty for the state and personally received the deathbed entrustment. His single-minded devotion was without equal and inspires awe through the ages.

sentences.zh: 此不待臣言，陛下備知之矣。

translations.literal: This does not await this subject's words—Your Majesty is fully aware.
translations.idiomatic: This needs no words from me. Your Majesty knows it fully already.

sentences.zh: 臣嘗有此心，未敢聞奏。

translations.literal: This subject once had this heart but did not dare report it to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: I have long felt this in my heart but did not dare report it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 且萬姓失業，旰食忘勞；

translations.literal: Moreover the myriad people have lost their livelihoods; late eating forgets fatigue;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the myriad people have lost their livelihoods, and Your Majesty eats late and forgets fatigue;

sentences.zh: 一物不安，納隍軫慮，在於微細，寧得過差。

translations.literal: if one thing is not at peace, you take to heart anxiety as if falling into a pit—in matters minute, how can there be excess error?
translations.idiomatic: if one thing is not at peace you take it to heart as if falling into a pit. In matters minute, how can there be excess error?

sentences.zh: 況社稷之舊臣，陛下之賢佐，無聞罪狀，斥去朝廷，內外氓黎，咸嗟舉措。

translations.literal: How much more an old minister of the altars of state, Your Majesty's worthy assistant—no crime heard of, yet expelled from court; within and without, the common people all sigh at the act.
translations.idiomatic: How much more when an old minister of the altars of state, Your Majesty's worthy assistant, is expelled from court with no crime heard against him. Within and without, the people all sigh at this act.

sentences.zh: 觀其近日言事，披誠懇切，詎肯後陛下之德，異於堯、舜；

translations.literal: Observing his recent words on affairs, he spread sincerity earnestly—how would he lag behind Your Majesty's virtue, differ from Yao and Shun;
translations.idiomatic: Judging from his recent remonstrance, he spoke with earnest sincerity. How could he wish to lag behind Your Majesty's virtue or differ from Yao and Shun?

sentences.zh: 懼陛下之過，塵於史冊。

translations.literal: he feared Your Majesty's fault would be dust on the historical records.
translations.idiomatic: He feared only that Your Majesty's fault would be recorded in the histories.

sentences.zh: 而乃深遭厚謗，重負丑言，可以痛志士之心，損陛下之明也。

translations.literal: Yet he deeply suffers heavy slander and bears again ugly words—this can pain the heart of men of purpose and harm Your Majesty's brightness.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he has suffered heavy slander and bears shameful accusations. This pains the hearts of loyal men and diminishes Your Majesty's reputation for wisdom.

sentences.zh: 臣聞晉武弘裕，不貽劉毅之誅；

translations.literal: This subject has heard that Emperor Wu of Jin was magnanimous and did not visit execution on Liu Yi;
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that Emperor Wu of Jin was magnanimous and did not execute Liu Yi;

sentences.zh: 漢祖深仁，無恚周昌之直。

translations.literal: the Han founder was deeply humane and bore no resentment toward Zhou Chang's bluntness.
translations.idiomatic: the Han founder was deeply humane and bore no resentment toward Zhou Chang's blunt remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 而遂良被遷，已經寒暑，違忤陛下，其罰塞焉。

translations.literal: Yet Suiliang has been transferred and already passed cold and heat; in opposing Your Majesty, his punishment is full.
translations.idiomatic: Suiliang has been transferred and has already passed a full year. In opposing Your Majesty he has been punished enough.

sentences.zh: 伏願纟面鑑無辜，稍寬非罪，俯矜微款，以順人情。

translations.literal: I bow and wish deep examination of the innocent, slight easing of wrongful guilt, bending to pity this humble plea, to accord with human feeling.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly beg Your Majesty to examine the case of an innocent man, ease his unjust punishment, and show pity for this humble plea so as to accord with the people's feelings.

sentences.zh: 疏奏，帝謂瑗曰：「遂良之情，朕亦知之矣。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, the emperor said to Yuan: "Suiliang's feelings—I also know them.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, the emperor said to Yuan, "I know Suiliang's feelings as well.

sentences.zh: 然其悖戾犯上，以此責之，朕豈有過，卿言何若是之深也！

translations.literal: Yet he was perverse and rebellious, offending his superiors—for this he is blamed. How could I have fault? Why are your words so deep as this!
translations.idiomatic: But he was perverse and rebellious in offending his sovereign. For this he is being punished. How could I be at fault? Why do you speak so strongly!

sentences.zh: 」瑗對曰：「遂良可謂社稷忠臣，臣恐以諛佞之輩，蒼蠅點白，損陷忠貞。

translations.literal: " Yuan replied: "Suiliang may be called a loyal minister of the altars of state. I fear that flatterers and sycophants, like bluebottles spotting white, will harm and trap the loyal and steadfast.
translations.idiomatic: " Yuan replied, "Suiliang may truly be called a loyal minister of the state. I fear that flatterers, like flies spotting white cloth, will slander and destroy the loyal and steadfast.

sentences.zh: 昔微子去之而殷國以亡，張華不死而綱紀不亂，國之慾謝，善人其衰。

translations.literal: Formerly when Weizi left, the Yin state perished; when Zhang Hua did not die, statutes and discipline were not disordered—when a state is about to decline, good men decay.
translations.idiomatic: When Weizi left, the Yin state perished. When Zhang Hua lived, order was preserved. When a state is about to fall, good men decline.

sentences.zh: 今陛下富有四海，八紘清泰，忽驅逐舊臣，而不垂省察乎！

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty is rich in the four seas and the eight cords are clear and peaceful—suddenly to drive out an old minister and not bend to examination!
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty possesses the four seas and the realm is at peace. Will you suddenly drive out an old minister without careful examination!

sentences.zh: 伏願違彼覆車，以收往過，垂勸誡於事君，則群生幸甚。

translations.literal: I bow and wish to avoid that overturned cart, to recover past errors, to bestow admonition on serving one's lord—then the multitude would be greatly fortunate.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly beg you to avoid the mistake of the overturned cart, correct past errors, and set an example of how to serve one's lord. Then the people would be greatly blessed.

sentences.zh: 」帝竟不納。

translations.literal: " The emperor in the end did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor in the end did not accept his advice.

sentences.zh: 瑗以言不見用，憂憤上表，請歸田裡，詔不許。

translations.literal: Because his words were not used, Yuan in grief and anger submitted a memorial requesting return to his fields; an edict did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Because his words were not heeded, Yuan submitted a memorial in grief and anger requesting retirement to his estate. The emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 顯慶二年，許敬宗、李義府希皇后之旨，誣奏瑗與褚遂良潛謀不軌，以桂州用武之地，故授遂良桂州刺史，實以為外援。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianqing, Xu Jingzong and Li Yifu, pleasing the empress's intent, falsely memorialized that Yuan and Chu Suiliang secretly plotted irregularity; because Guizhou was a place of military deployment they therefore appointed Suiliang prefect of Guizhou, in reality as external aid.
translations.idiomatic: In 657 Xu Jingzong and Li Yifu, acting on the empress's wishes, falsely memorialized that Yuan and Chu Suiliang had plotted rebellion. Because Guizhou was a strategic military region, they had appointed Suiliang prefect of Guizhou as external support for the plot.

sentences.zh: 於是更貶遂良為愛州刺史，左授瑗振州刺史。

translations.literal: Thereupon Suiliang was further demoted to prefect of Aizhou and Yuan was demoted to prefect of Zhenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Suiliang was further demoted to prefect of Aizhou and Yuan was demoted to prefect of Zhenzhou.

sentences.zh: 四年，卒官，年五十四。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he died in office, aged fifty-four.
translations.idiomatic: In 659 he died in office at the age of fifty-four.

sentences.zh: 明年，長孫無忌死，敬宗等又奏瑗與無忌通謀，遣使殺之。

translations.literal: The next year Zhangsun Wuji died; Jingzong and others again memorialized that Yuan had conspired with Wuji and sent envoys to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Zhangsun Wuji died. Jingzong and others again memorialized that Yuan had conspired with Wuji and sent envoys to kill him.

sentences.zh: 及使至，瑗已死，更發棺驗屍而還，籍沒其家，孫配徙嶺表。

translations.literal: When the envoys arrived Yuan was already dead; they again opened the coffin and examined the corpse and returned; his household goods were confiscated and his grandson was banished to south of the ranges.
translations.idiomatic: When the envoys arrived Yuan was already dead. They opened his coffin to verify the corpse, confiscated his family's property, and banished his grandson to the far south.

sentences.zh: 神龍元年，則天遺制令復其官爵。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shenlong, Empress Wu's deathbed decree ordered restoration of his offices and titles.
translations.idiomatic: In 705 Empress Wu's deathbed decree ordered restoration of his offices and titles.

sentences.zh: =來濟=

translations.literal: =Lai Ji=
translations.idiomatic: Lai Ji

sentences.zh: 來濟，揚州江都人，隋左翊衛大將軍榮國公護子也。

translations.literal: Lai Ji was a man of Jiangdu in Yangzhou, son of Hu, Duke of Rong of Sui, Grand General of the Left Wing Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Lai Ji was a native of Jiangdu in Yangzhou, son of Hu, Duke of Rong, who had served as grand general of the left wing guard under the Sui.

sentences.zh: 宇文化及之難，闔門遇害。

translations.literal: In the disaster of Yuwen Huaji, the whole household met calamity.
translations.idiomatic: In the disaster wrought by Yuwen Huaji, his entire household was killed.

sentences.zh: 濟幼逢家難，流離艱險，而篤志好學，有文詞，善談論，尤曉時務。

translations.literal: Ji from youth met family disaster, drifting through hardship and peril, yet with firm resolve loved learning; he had literary compositions, was skilled in discourse, and especially understood current affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Ji suffered family disaster in youth and drifted through hardship, yet he studied with firm resolve. He had literary talent, was skilled in discourse, and especially understood current affairs.

sentences.zh: 舉進士，貞觀中累轉通事舍人。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination; in Zhenguan he rose in succession to Master of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and during the Zhenguan era rose to master of ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 太子承乾之敗，太宗謂侍臣曰：「欲何以處承乾？

translations.literal: When Crown Prince Chengqian failed, Taizong said to the attending ministers: "How do you wish to deal with Chengqian?
translations.idiomatic: When Crown Prince Chengqian was deposed, Taizong asked his attending ministers, "What should be done with Chengqian?

sentences.zh: 」群臣莫敢對，濟進曰：「陛下上不失作慈父，下得盡天年，即為善矣。

translations.literal: " The ministers dared not reply; Ji advanced and said: "Above, Your Majesty would not fail as a loving father; below, he could complete his natural years—that would be good.
translations.idiomatic: " No minister dared reply. Ji stepped forward and said, "If above Your Majesty does not fail as a loving father and below he may live out his natural years, that would be best.

sentences.zh: 」帝納其言。

translations.literal: " The emperor accepted his words.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor accepted his advice.

sentences.zh: 俄除考功員外郎。

translations.literal: Shortly he was made Vice Director in the Bureau of Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was appointed vice director in the Bureau of Appointments.

sentences.zh: 十八年，初置太子司議郎，妙選人望，遂以濟為之，仍兼崇賢館直學士。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year the crown prince's Reviewer was first established; men of outstanding reputation were finely selected, and Ji was made such, also serving concurrently as academician-director of the Chongxian Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In 644 the office of crown prince reviewer was first established. Men of outstanding reputation were selected, and Ji was appointed to the post while also serving as academician-director of the Chongxian Hall.

sentences.zh: 尋遷中書舍人，與令狐德棻等撰《晉書》。

translations.literal: Shortly he was moved to Secretariat Draftsman and with Linghu Defen and others compiled the Book of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was promoted to secretariat draftsman and with Linghu Defen and others compiled the Book of Jin.

sentences.zh: 永徽二年，拜中書侍郎，兼弘文館學士，監修國史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yonghui he was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat, concurrently academician of the Hongwen Hall, supervising compilation of the national history.
translations.idiomatic: In 651 he was appointed vice director of the Secretariat, concurrently academician of the Hongwen Hall, and put in charge of compiling the national history.

sentences.zh: 四年，同中書門下三品。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was given the same third rank at Secretariat-Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: In 653 he was given third rank at the Secretariat-Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 五年，加銀青光祿大夫，以修國史功封南陽縣男，賜物七百段。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was made Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Silver Seal; for merit in compiling the national history he was enfeoffed as Baron of Nanyang County and granted seven hundred rolls of goods.
translations.idiomatic: In 654 he was made grand master of splendid happiness with silver seal. For compiling the national history he was enfeoffed as baron of Nanyang County and granted seven hundred rolls of goods.

sentences.zh: 六年，遷中書令、檢校吏部尚書。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was moved to Chief of the Secretariat and acting Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In 655 he was promoted to chief of the Secretariat and acting minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 時高宗欲立昭儀武氏為宸妃，濟密表諫曰：「宸妃古無此號，事將不可。

translations.literal: At the time Gaozong wished to establish Lady Wu of the Bright Countenance as Lady of the Inner Quarters; Ji submitted a secret memorial remonstrating: "The Lady of the Inner Quarters—antiquity had no such title; the matter cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Gaozong wished to establish Lady Wu as Lady of the Inner Quarters. Ji submitted a secret memorial: "Antiquity had no such title. The matter cannot be done.

sentences.zh: 」武皇后既立，濟等懼不自安；

translations.literal: " After Empress Wu was established, Ji and others feared and were ill at ease;
translations.idiomatic: " After Empress Wu was established, Ji and others lived in fear;

sentences.zh: 後乃抗表稱濟忠公，請加賞慰，而心實惡之。

translations.literal: later she submitted a defiant memorial calling Ji loyal and fair and requesting added reward and consolation, yet in heart truly hated him.
translations.idiomatic: later she submitted a memorial praising Ji as loyal and fair and requesting that he be rewarded, though in her heart she hated him.

sentences.zh: 顯慶元年，兼太子賓客，進爵為侯，中書令如故。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianqing he served concurrently as Mentor of the Crown Prince, advanced in rank to marquis, Chief of the Secretariat as before.
translations.idiomatic: In 656 he served concurrently as mentor of the crown prince, was advanced to marquis, and retained his post as chief of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 二年，又兼太子詹事。

translations.literal: In the second year he also served concurrently as Steward of the Crown Prince's Household.
translations.idiomatic: In 657 he also served concurrently as steward of the crown prince's household.

sentences.zh: 尋而許敬宗等奏濟與褚遂良朋黨構扇，左授台州刺史。

translations.literal: Shortly Xu Jingzong and others memorialized that Ji had formed a faction with Chu Suiliang and incited trouble; he was demoted to prefect of Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Xu Jingzong and others memorialized that Ji had formed a faction with Chu Suiliang and incited trouble. He was demoted to prefect of Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 五年，徙庭州刺史。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was transferred to prefect of Tingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In 660 he was transferred to prefect of Tingzhou.

sentences.zh: 龍朔二年，突厥入寇，濟總兵拒之，謂其眾曰：「吾嘗掛刑網，蒙赦性命，當以身塞責，特報國恩。

translations.literal: In the second year of Longshuo the Turks invaded; Ji commanded the army to resist them and said to his troops: "I once hung in the penal net and received pardon of life—I should with my person block responsibility and specially repay the state's grace.
translations.idiomatic: In 662 the Turks invaded. Ji commanded the army to resist them and told his troops, "I once faced execution and was pardoned. I must repay the state's grace with my life.

sentences.zh: 」遂不釋甲冑赴賊，沒於陣。

translations.literal: " Thereupon without removing armor he went toward the enemy and perished in the battle line.
translations.idiomatic: " He did not remove his armor and charged the enemy, dying in battle.

sentences.zh: 時年五十三，贈楚州刺史，給靈輿遞還鄉。

translations.literal: He was then fifty-three; posthumously made prefect of Chuzhou and given a funeral carriage relayed back to his home.
translations.idiomatic: He was fifty-three. Posthumously he was made prefect of Chuzhou, and his body was conveyed home in a state funeral carriage.

sentences.zh: 有文集三十捲，行於代。

translations.literal: He had a collected works in thirty juan, current in his generation.
translations.idiomatic: His collected works in thirty juan circulated in his time.

sentences.zh: 兄 亙濟兄亙，有學行，與濟齊名。
