translations.literal: Elder brother Gen—Ji's elder brother Gen had learning and conduct and was equally famous with Ji.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Gen had learning and integrity and was as famous as Ji.

sentences.zh: 上元中，官至黃門侍郎、同中書門下三品。

translations.literal: In Shangyuan he reached Vice Director of the Yellow Gate and the same third rank at Secretariat-Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shangyuan era he rose to vice director of the Yellow Gate with third rank at the Secretariat-Chancellery.

sentences.zh: =上官儀=

translations.literal: =Shangguan Yi=
translations.idiomatic: Shangguan Yi

sentences.zh: 上官儀，本陝州陝人也。

translations.literal: Shangguan Yi was originally a man of Shan in Shanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shangguan Yi was originally a native of Shan in Shanzhou.

sentences.zh: 父弘，隋江都宮副監，因家於江都。

translations.literal: His father Hong was deputy director of the Jiangdu palace in Sui; the family settled in Jiangdu.
translations.idiomatic: His father Hong served as deputy director of the Jiangdu palace under the Sui, and the family settled in Jiangdu.

sentences.zh: 大業末，弘為將軍陳稜所殺，儀時幼，藏匿獲免。

translations.literal: At the end of Daye, Hong was killed by the general Chen Suo; Yi was then young and by hiding escaped.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Daye era Hong was killed by the general Chen Suo. Yi was still young and escaped by hiding.

sentences.zh: 因私度為沙門，游情釋典，尤精《三論》，兼涉獵經史，善屬文。

translations.literal: Thereupon he privately took tonsure as a monk, roamed in feeling through Buddhist scriptures, was especially expert in the Three Treatises, and also ranged through the classics and histories, skilled at literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: He then privately became a monk, immersed himself in Buddhist scriptures, and was especially expert in the Three Treatises. He also studied the classics and histories and was skilled at literary composition.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，楊仁恭為都督，深禮待之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguan Yang Rengong was area commander and treated him with deep courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Zhenguan era Yang Rengong was area commander and treated him with great respect.

sentences.zh: 舉進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 太宗聞其名，召授弘文館直學士。

translations.literal: Taizong heard his name and summoned him, appointing him academician-director of the Hongwen Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong heard of him and appointed him academician-director of the Hongwen Hall.

sentences.zh: 累遷秘書郎。

translations.literal: He rose in succession to secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to secretary.

sentences.zh: 時太宗雅好屬文，每遣儀視草，又多令繼和，凡有宴集，儀嘗預焉。

translations.literal: At the time Taizong elegantly loved literary composition; he often sent Yi to review drafts and also often ordered him to continue and harmonize; whenever there were banquets and gatherings, Yi was often present.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong loved literary composition. He often had Yi review his drafts and compose matching verses. Yi was a regular guest at court banquets.

sentences.zh: 俄又預撰《晉書》成，轉起居郎，加級賜帛。

translations.literal: Shortly he also participated in compiling the Book of Jin to completion, was transferred to diarist of the imperial presence, and was given a grade promotion and silk.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he took part in completing the Book of Jin, was transferred to diarist of the imperial presence, and received a promotion in rank and a gift of silk.

sentences.zh: 高宗嗣位，遷秘書少監。

translations.literal: When Gaozong succeeded to the throne he was moved to vice director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozong succeeded to the throne he was promoted to vice director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 龍朔二年，加銀青光祿大夫、西台侍郎、同東西台三品，兼弘文館學士如故。

translations.literal: In the second year of Longshuo he was made Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Silver Seal, Vice Director of the Western Terrace, same third rank at East and West Terraces, and concurrently academician of the Hongwen Hall as before.
translations.idiomatic: In 662 he was made grand master of splendid happiness with silver seal, vice director of the Western Terrace, with third rank at the Eastern and Western Terraces, and retained his post as academician of the Hongwen Hall.

sentences.zh: 本以詞彩自達，工於五言詩，好以綺錯婉媚為本。

translations.literal: Originally he distinguished himself through literary color, was accomplished in five-character poetry, and liked to take brocade-like intricacy and graceful charm as his foundation.
translations.idiomatic: He had distinguished himself through literary brilliance, was accomplished in five-character poetry, and favored ornate and graceful style as his foundation.

sentences.zh: 儀既貴顯，故當時多有效其體者，時人謂為上官體。

translations.literal: Once Yi was noble and prominent, many at the time imitated his style; people of the time called it the Shangguan style.
translations.idiomatic: Once Yi had risen to high rank, many imitated his style, which people called the Shangguan style.

sentences.zh: 儀頗恃才任勢，故為當代所嫉。

translations.literal: Yi rather relied on talent and wielded power, and therefore was envied by his contemporaries.
translations.idiomatic: Yi relied on his talent and wielded his power, and was envied by his contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 麟德元年，宦者王伏勝與梁王忠抵罪，許敬宗乃構儀與忠通謀，遂下獄而死，家口籍沒。

translations.literal: In the first year of Linde the eunuch Wang Fusheng and Prince of Liang Zhong met guilt; Xu Jingzong then framed Yi as having conspired with Zhong; he was put in prison and died, and his household was confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: In 664 the eunuch Wang Fusheng and Prince Zhong of Liang were convicted of crimes. Xu Jingzong framed Yi as having conspired with Zhong. Yi was imprisoned and died, and his household was confiscated.

sentences.zh: 子庭芝，歷位周王府屬。

translations.literal: His son Tingzhi held posts as an official of the Prince of Zhou's household.
translations.idiomatic: His son Tingzhi served as an official in the household of the Prince of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 與儀俱被殺。

translations.literal: He was killed together with Yi.
translations.idiomatic: He was killed together with Yi.

sentences.zh: 庭芝有女，中宗時為昭容，每侍帝草制誥，以故追贈儀為中書令、秦州都督、楚國公；

translations.literal: Tingzhi had a daughter who in Zhongzong's time was a Lady of the Bright Countenance; she often attended the emperor in drafting edicts—therefore Yi was posthumously made Chief of the Secretariat, area commander of Qinzhou, and Duke of Chu;
translations.idiomatic: Tingzhi had a daughter who under Emperor Zhongzong served as Lady of the Bright Countenance and often helped the emperor draft edicts. For this reason Yi was posthumously made chief of the Secretariat, area commander of Qinzhou, and Duke of Chu;

sentences.zh: 庭芝黃門侍郎、岐州刺史、天水郡公，仍令以禮改葬。

translations.literal: Tingzhi was made Vice Director of the Yellow Gate, prefect of Qizhou, and Duke of Tianshui Commandery, and they were still ordered reburied according to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Tingzhi was made vice director of the Yellow Gate, prefect of Qizhou, and duke of Tianshui Commandery, and both were ordered reburied with full honors.

sentences.zh: =史臣曰=

translations.literal: =The Historian says=
translations.idiomatic: The Historian's Commentary

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：褚河南上書言事，亹癖有經世遠略。

translations.literal: The Historian says: Chu of Henan in memorials on affairs was diligent and had far-reaching plans to order the age.
translations.idiomatic: The historian says: Chu Suiliang of Henan, in his memorials on affairs of state, was diligent and possessed far-reaching plans for governing the realm.

sentences.zh: 魏徵、王珪之後，骨鯁風彩，落落負王佐器者，殆難其人。

translations.literal: After Wei Zheng and Wang Gui, in bone and spine and wind and color, openly bearing the vessel of a king's assistant—hardly could one find his equal.
translations.idiomatic: After Wei Zheng and Wang Gui, among those who bore the bearing of a true minister and openly possessed the capacity of a king's assistant, his equal was hard to find.

sentences.zh: 名臣事業，河南有焉。

translations.literal: Among famous ministers' achievements, Henan had his share.
translations.idiomatic: Among the achievements of famous ministers, Chu of Henan had his place.

sentences.zh: 昔齊人饋樂而仲尼去，戎王溺妓而由余奔，婦人之言，聖哲懼罹其禍，況二佞據衡軸之地，為正人之魑魅乎！

translations.literal: Formerly when the men of Qi presented music Confucius left; when the Rong king drowned in entertainers Youyu fled—a woman's words, the sage and wise feared encountering their calamity; how much more when two flatterers occupied the pivot's place, becoming bogies to upright men!
translations.idiomatic: When the men of Qi presented music, Confucius departed. When the Rong king drowned himself in entertainers, Youyu fled. Even sages feared the calamity of a woman's words. How much more when two flatterers held the pivot of power and became demons to upright men!

sentences.zh: 古之志士仁人，一言相期，死不之悔，況於君臣之間，受託孤之寄，而以利害禍福，忘平生之言哉！

translations.literal: The men of purpose and humanity of antiquity, with one word pledged to each other, did not regret unto death—how much more between lord and minister, receiving the deathbed entrustment, yet by gain and loss, calamity and fortune, forgetting words of a lifetime!
translations.idiomatic: Men of purpose and humanity in antiquity, once they pledged themselves with a single word, did not regret it even unto death. How much more between lord and minister, when one has received a deathbed entrustment, can one forget one's lifelong pledge for the sake of gain, loss, or personal safety!

sentences.zh: 而韓、來諸公，可謂守死善道，求福不回者焉。

translations.literal: Yet the gentlemen Han, Lai, and the rest may be called those who kept death and the good Way, seeking blessing without turning back.
translations.idiomatic: Han Yuan, Lai Ji, and the others may truly be called men who held to the good Way unto death and sought no blessing by turning back.

translations.literal: =Eulogy=
translations.idiomatic: Eulogy

sentences.zh: 贊曰：褚公之言，和樂愔愔，鐘石在虡，動成雅音。

translations.literal: The eulogy says: Lord Chu's words were harmonious and joyful, gentle and calm; bell and stone on the stand—when moved they formed elegant sound.
translations.idiomatic: The eulogy says: Lord Chu's words were harmonious and serene; like bells and stones on their stand, when struck they formed elegant music.

sentences.zh: 二猘雙吠，三賢一心。

translations.literal: Two mad dogs barked in pair; three worthies were one in heart.
translations.idiomatic: Two mad dogs barked together; three worthies were of one heart.

sentences.zh: 人皆觀望，我不浮沉。

translations.literal: All men watched and waited; I did not float or sink.
translations.idiomatic: While others watched and waited, I would not drift with the tide.
